title: Digital Asset Accounting
answer: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation, token valuation, contract auditing, decentralised treasuries and impairment.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation
children.blurb: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation is the process of matching on-chain transactions and balances to the entries in a company's accounting ledger.

children.name: Valuing Illiquid Tokens
children.blurb: Valuing illiquid tokens covers the accounting and reporting work needed when a digital asset has no reliable, active market price.

children.name: Auditing Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Auditing smart contracts is the review of self-executing code on a blockchain to find defects, security flaws, and mismatches between what the code does and what its users or owners believe it does.

children.name: Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries
children.blurb: Accounting for decentralised treasuries covers the recognition, measurement, and reporting of assets and liabilities held by DAOs, protocol foundations, and other on-chain organisations that control funds through smart contracts and multisignature wallets.

children.name: Impairment of Unique Digital Assets
children.blurb: Impairment of unique digital assets covers non-fungible tokens, tokenized collectibles, digital art, virtual land, in-game items, and other distinct on-chain assets that are not interchangeable.

sections.body: Digital asset accounting is the work of recording, valuing, and reporting blockchain based assets and obligations in a general ledger. AI is used in practice to match on chain transfers with internal entries, flag anomalies, and classify wallets and tokens at scale. It also helps parse smart contract events, estimate fair value for tokens with thin markets, and test contract logic against accounting rules. For decentralised treasuries, models can trace inflows and outflows across many addresses and propose journal entries for human review. For unique digital assets, AI can group similar items, detect duplicates, and support impairment testing when markets are sparse. The work is still accounting, so the output is a draft, a flag, or a valuation range, not an audited number.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Reconciliation is the most mature area, because blockchains give a complete transaction log and AI is good at matching messy labels to ledger accounts. Valuation of illiquid tokens remains hard, since prices can be manipulated, markets can be thin, and comparable sales may not exist. Smart contract auditing has advanced with automated tools, but formal verification and economic security still need human judgement. Decentralised treasury accounting is not solved, because governance votes, multisig controls, and token grants often lack clean accounting treatment. Impairment of unique digital assets is also unsettled, as fair value can swing and there is no single accepted model for every collectible or virtual land parcel. The site's 219 compliance and regulation pages sit nearby because token rules vary by jurisdiction, and the honest limits are data quality and the fact that AI can suggest but cannot sign off.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section move from raw chain data to reporting judgements. Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation is the entry point for matching wallets, exchanges, and custody accounts to the books. Valuing Illiquid Tokens then deals with price discovery when no reliable market exists, and Auditing Smart Contracts covers code review, event logs, and control testing. Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries extends those ideas to multisig wallets, governance tokens, and community grants. Impairment of Unique Digital Assets closes the loop on non fungible items, where carrying value and write downs need support. Read together, they show how AI assists each step, and where a human accountant still has to decide.
